newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Boral sees higher prices, margins.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Boral sees higher prices, margins.

text.p: Building materials and energy group Boral Ltd said on Wednesday that an upturn in the home building sector was expected to raise prices and margins for Boral's building materials products.

"Along with increased sales there will be a positive effect on margins because the high fixed costs will be spread more widely," Boral managing director Tony Berg told reporters after releasing the group's first half result.
"Prices will improve as a result of the upturn as well," he said.
Berg said Boral was seeing an improvement in building approvals, but that this had yet to flow through into significant new demand for building materials.
"We are expecting the upturn to emerge in the June quarter of this year," Berg said.
"We see further growth in the non-dwelling and infrastructure areas which will benefit the construction materials sector," he said.
"We're expecting an improvement (in the second half of 1996/97) half on half in the building products sector that caters to the dwelling market."

Berg also said interest costs would be lower in the second half because of asset sales in previous periods which had been used to reduce debt and cut gearing to about 51 percent currently from 59 percent at June 30, 1996.
Earlier Boral reported a A$93.16 million net profit for the six months to December 31, down from A$169.71 million in the same period a year earlier.
Net profit pre-abnormals fell to A$96 million from A$120 million the previous year and compared with market expectations for a pre-abnormals net of about A$90 million.
Pre-tax and interest earnings (EBIT) fell to A$221 million from A$245 million.
Boral also said it expected the second half to be ahead of the same period a year earlier.
Berg said he would not comment on whether the full 1996/97 year pre-abnormals net profit would be above the A$170.9 million achieved a year earlier.
But he said it was unlikely the second half result would be better than the first half because of the usual seasonal patterns in the January to June period.
Housing construction tended to slow in January and February months in Australian and the United States because it was the heart of the summer and winter respectively, he said.
Boral posted a A$51 million pre-abnormal net profit in the second half of 1995/96.
Boral shares were down one cent at A$3.43 at 11.50 p.m. (0050 GMT).
